question: Can residuals of finite-dimensional Koopman models provide one mechanistically interpretable early-warning signal for both bifurcation-induced tipping and rate-induced tipping, including in a coupled-climate-model AMOC ensemble?

key_findings.claim: The paper gives bifurcation- and rate-induced tipping distinct residual mechanisms inside one Koopman framework, but proves only a conditional lower bound for the rate-induced case rather than universal residual growth.
key_findings.evidence: Near a bifurcation, the autonomous ResKMD residual is decomposed into truncation and stochastic-fluctuation terms, with slow Koopman modes approaching the unit circle. For a nonautonomous system augmented by its control, Theorem 1 lower-bounds the control-aware residual by unresolved attractor-branch drift minus unresolved higher-order terms when local restoring dynamics are represented. Remark 1 and the supplement construct the countercase: exact closure of the augmented observable dynamics can make the residual zero even while the trajectory fails to track the moving attractor.

anchors.section: When residual divergence need not occur

key_findings.claim: Across four prototype bifurcation- and rate-induced systems, Koopman residuals usually discriminate tipping trajectories better than standard critical-slowing-down statistics, especially when the observable dictionary is learned.
key_findings.evidence: The May harvesting fold and Rosenzweig-MacArthur Hopf experiments use 50 tipping and 50 non-tipping realizations each; the forced saddle-node and Bautin experiments split trajectories by forcing rate. Windowed AUROC and Kendall-tau comparisons show the Koopman indicators rising before transition while variance and lag-1 autocorrelation are much less reliable for rate-induced tipping. Random Fourier, delay-coordinate, and MLP-autoencoder dictionaries are compared, and the learned representation is strongest on the higher-dimensional cases.

anchors.section: Koopman EWS skills on prototypical systems
Koopman EWS skills on prototypical systems

key_findings.claim: The residual signal transfers qualitatively to five single-transition empirical datasets, but these examples do not establish calibrated prospective discrimination.
key_findings.evidence: On a microcosm collapse, human voice onset, cellular ATP depletion, a greenhouse-Earth transition, and a power-grid blackout, one or more Koopman dictionaries produce a pre-event rise that is earlier or clearer than variance or lag-1 autocorrelation. Because each record supplies essentially one transition and no matched non-tipping population, the evidence is visual and temporal rather than an AUROC estimate or a false-alarm analysis.

key_findings.claim: Control augmentation is necessary in the paper's rate-forced AMOC box-model experiment, whereas the autonomous residual is most effective in the bifurcation-forced version.
key_findings.evidence: The same low-order AMOC model is driven once toward a quasi-static bifurcation and once quickly enough to lose tracking. Autonomous ResKMD provides the clearer warning in the former; conditioning the observable map on the time-varying freshwater forcing exposes the tracking-error residual in the latter, matching the mechanism predicted by the decomposition.

anchors.section: AMOC tipping in a box model
AMOC tipping in a box model

key_findings.claim: In the ten-member NASA GISS-E2.1-G SSP2-4.5 ensemble, the control-aware learned-observable residual separates the two weak-branch members from the eight non-tipping members well before the diagnosed transition, but the positive sample is too small for a stable operating characteristic.
key_findings.evidence: Annual AMOC strength near 48 degrees north is paired with a smoothed Denmark Strait sea-ice freshwater-flux control. The control-aware MLP residual begins a persistent rise around 2150 in the two members that later enter the weak circulation branch, while it remains lower for the other eight. The analysis uses only two positive members and selects a physically motivated control after examining alternatives, so it is an existence demonstration rather than population-level validation.

anchors.section: AMOC tipping in a coupled climate model

key_findings.claim: Spectral diagnostics and the residual carry complementary information, and the coupled-model conclusion is sensitive to what is supplied as the control.
key_findings.evidence: Tipping members show discrete Koopman eigenvalues moving outward and slow generator modes approaching zero more rapidly, yet the single slowest e-folding time can be larger in non-tipping members. A supplementary ablation replacing Denmark Strait freshwater flux with mixed-layer depth in four basins materially changes warning behavior, demonstrating that a plausible but dynamically incomplete control can alter the result.

method.core_idea: Fit local finite-dimensional Koopman operators in rolling windows and use their normalized one-step residual as a measure of dynamics not represented by the current observable subspace; for rate-induced tipping, augment that subspace with the external control so unresolved failure to follow a moving attractor enters the residual.
method.mechanism: Extended dynamic mode decomposition regresses an observable dictionary at one time against the next. The autonomous score is a residual dynamic-mode-decomposition quantity; the control-aware score uses observables of state and forcing. Dictionaries include 500 random Fourier features, a 20-lag time-delay embedding, and a neural encoder trained on the first window and then frozen. Singular-vector truncation retains modes explaining 90% of energy. Scores are computed in moving windows, compared with variance and lag-1 autocorrelation using Kendall trend and AUROC, and supplemented by Koopman eigenvalue, spectral-gap, generator-mode, and e-folding-time diagnostics.
assumptions: Successive samples are rich and stationary enough within each rolling window for an EDMD operator and residual to be estimated meaningfully.
The retained observable dictionary captures local restoring dynamics while excluding enough attractor-branch drift or nonlinear correction for rate-induced loss of tracking to appear in the residual.
A measured exogenous control is available, correctly timed, and sufficiently close to the variable driving the moving attractor.
For the bifurcation interpretation, relevant Koopman point-spectrum modes exist and approach the unit circle as local recovery slows.
Tipping and non-tipping trajectory labels, including the coupled-model weak-AMOC classification, identify the dynamical event the score is intended to anticipate.
Training a neural observable map on the first window and freezing it gives a stable coordinate system rather than an early-window representation that becomes out of distribution later.

techniques.role: Measures normalized one-step dynamics left outside a locally fitted Koopman-invariant observable subspace.
Conditions the Koopman approximation on the external forcing so unexplained moving-branch tracking dynamics can contribute to the score.
Uses a frozen MLP autoencoder to discover observables that represent high-dimensional local dynamics more compactly than prescribed features.
Retains modes accounting for 90% of observable energy, making unresolved dynamics explicit in the residual.
Evaluates warning time series with Kendall trend and AUROC over matched tipping and non-tipping simulations.
Checks residual changes against discrete eigenvalue motion, generator modes, gaps, and e-folding times rather than interpreting a scalar score alone.
Substitutes candidate climate controls to expose the dependence of the rate-induced signal on control specification.

evaluations.setting: Stochastic May harvesting fold and Rosenzweig-MacArthur Hopf systems, 50 tipping and 50 non-tipping realizations per system
evaluations.metric: Pre-transition Kendall tau and AUROC in rolling windows
evaluations.result: Residual-based Koopman indicators rise consistently and generally attain the strongest discrimination; learned observables are especially effective in the higher-dimensional setting
evaluations.baseline: Lag-1 autocorrelation, variance, random Fourier features, and delay-coordinate dictionaries

evaluations.setting: Forced saddle-node and Bautin systems with tipping determined by forcing rate
evaluations.result: Control-aware Koopman residuals warn under rate-induced loss of tracking, where classical critical-slowing-down signals are inconsistent
evaluations.baseline: Autonomous residual, variance, and lag-1 autocorrelation

evaluations.setting: Five empirical transition records spanning ecology, physiology, cellular metabolism, climate, and power systems
evaluations.metric: Qualitative lead and monotonic rise before the known event
evaluations.result: At least one Koopman dictionary gives an earlier or clearer rise across all five examples
evaluations.baseline: Variance and lag-1 autocorrelation; no matched non-event cohort or calibrated false-alarm rate

evaluations.setting: Low-order AMOC box model under quasi-static and rapid freshwater forcing
evaluations.result: Autonomous residual is strongest for bifurcation forcing; control-aware residual is strongest for rate forcing
evaluations.baseline: The opposite residual formulation and classical critical-slowing-down statistics

evaluations.setting: Ten-member GISS-E2.1-G SSP2-4.5 ensemble, annual 48N AMOC, two weak-branch members
evaluations.metric: Residual trajectory and spectral trends before the diagnosed transition
evaluations.result: The control-aware MLP residual begins separating the two eventual weak-branch members around 2150; slow generator modes also approach zero faster
evaluations.baseline: Eight non-tipping members, autonomous residual, and conventional spectral summaries

evaluations.metric: Qualitative persistence and separation of the warning signal
evaluations.result: Denmark Strait sea-ice freshwater flux produces the main reported pattern, while mixed-layer-depth controls in four basins yield materially different behavior

limitations: Author-stated: a rate-induced tipping event need not make the control-aware residual diverge; if the augmented observable system closes exactly, tracking can fail while the residual remains zero.

Author-stated: the theory assumes a suitable Koopman point spectrum and a dictionary that captures local restoration but leaves branch drift unresolved; not every nonlinear or strongly nonstationary system has this structure.
Author-stated: indicator quality depends on the observable dictionary, window length, truncation, sampling, noise, and the selected control variable.
Author-stated: the coupled GISS ensemble has only two tipping members, preventing reliable significance, threshold, false-positive, or lead-time estimates.
Reviewer-identified: the five empirical records are retrospective single-event demonstrations without matched non-events, so visual pre-event rises cannot establish prospective utility.

Reviewer-identified: choosing Denmark Strait flux as the main control after testing several plausible forcings introduces researcher degrees of freedom that require an independent ensemble for confirmation.
Reviewer-identified: the MLP observable map is trained only on the first window and frozen; later residual growth can therefore mix dynamical novelty with ordinary representation shift.

Reviewer-identified: defining coupled-model tipping by entry into a weak AMOC branch and evaluating on the same ten members does not test transport across models, scenarios, resolutions, or observational products.
Reviewer-identified: no operational threshold, uncertainty interval, calibration curve, or cost-weighted false-alarm analysis is supplied for climate deployment.
failure_modes: Exact finite-dimensional closure of the state-control observable dynamics suppresses the residual even when the physical trajectory no longer tracks its moving attractor.
An omitted, lagged, noisy, or merely correlated control can turn exogenous drift into unexplained residual or hide the actual forcing, creating false alarms or misses.
A dictionary that is too expressive absorbs branch drift and removes the warning; one that is too weak produces a persistently large approximation residual unrelated to tipping.
Short windows inflate finite-sample residual variance, whereas long windows average over the local change the indicator is meant to detect.
Noise, irregular sampling, sensor drift, or a changing observation operator can mimic unresolved dynamics.
Truncation by explained energy can discard low-energy but dynamically critical modes or retain nuisance modes.
A frozen learned representation can become out of distribution under climate drift, so its residual may detect encoder mismatch rather than loss of stability.
Post hoc selection among forcing variables, latitudes, smoothers, and dictionaries can overfit a very small ensemble.
Critical transitions without an approaching point-spectrum mode, or events driven by shocks rather than progressive drift, need not produce the proposed precursor.
reusable_insights: Separate warning mechanisms by causal route: autonomous recovery loss for bifurcations and control-conditioned tracking error for rate-induced transitions.
State explicitly what a residual can and cannot certify; unresolved dynamics are not logically equivalent to impending failure.
Use matched tipping and non-tipping trajectories to estimate false alarms, not just monotonicity before known events.
Freeze representation learning when auditing temporal residuals, but add a representation-shift control so nonstationarity is not mistaken for dynamics.
Triangulate a scalar warning score with spectral quantities and physical state variables because different summaries can move in opposite directions.
Pre-register the control-selection rule or validate it out of sample whenever the method conditions on a physically chosen forcing.
Treat dictionary size and truncation as an identifiability tradeoff: the warning exists only in dynamics deliberately left unresolved.
open_questions: What observable-selection criterion preserves local restoring modes while guaranteeing that moving-attractor drift remains detectable?
Can uncertainty-aware residual thresholds be calibrated across climate models and scenarios with realistic event rarity?
How can one distinguish true unresolved tracking dynamics from neural-dictionary distribution shift or sensor drift?
Does a multivariate or causally discovered control set outperform hand-selected single controls without overfitting?
How early and how consistently does the signal lead AMOC collapse in larger perturbed-physics and multi-model ensembles?
Can the no-divergence counterexample be converted into a practical identifiability test that warns when the indicator is theoretically blind?
How do irregular sampling, missing observations, and colored nonstationary noise affect the finite-sample residual distribution?

competitive_landscape.title: Generalized Stochastic Resilience for Early Warning Signals Based on Koopman Operator
competitive_landscape.difference: Miyauchi et al. introduce the stochastic ResKMD warning score, connect residual divergence to critical slowing down, and test synthetic and empirical bifurcation cases. This paper directly extends that machinery to measured controls and rate-induced tracking failure, and adds low-order plus coupled-model AMOC studies; its own theorem also narrows the claim by showing that rate-induced residual growth is conditional.

competitive_landscape.title: Early-warning indicators for rate-induced tipping
competitive_landscape.difference: Ritchie and Sieber analyze variance and autocorrelation along most-likely paths near rate-induced tipping in a saddle-node system. The present work replaces system-specific classical statistics with a data-driven control-aware Koopman residual across saddle-node, Bautin, and AMOC settings, but requires a suitable observed control and dictionary.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Learning for predicting rate-induced tipping
competitive_landscape.difference: Huang et al. train an explainable deep classifier to predict transition probabilities in three noisy rate-forced prototype systems. The Koopman method produces an interpretable residual and spectrum without a supervised tipping classifier and covers both bifurcation and rate mechanisms, but it does not output calibrated probabilities and is sensitive to control specification.

competitive_landscape.title: Anticipating AMOC transitions via deep learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. use a convolutional network on a calibrated AMOC box-model ensemble to predict individual transition probabilities across bifurcation-, rate-, and noise-induced regimes. This paper supplies operator-level mechanisms and tests a ten-member coupled GCM ensemble, but its two positive members cannot support the probability calibration and broad perturbation tests of the box-model study.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond expectations: Residual Dynamic Mode Decomposition and Variance for Stochastic Dynamical Systems
competitive_landscape.difference: Colbrook et al. develop stochastic residual DMD, variance decompositions, and verified spectral calculations for random dynamical systems. The present paper repurposes residual DMD as an early-warning statistic and augments it with controls; it does not match the prior work's general spectral verification theory.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: a single generalized Koopman framework explains and detects both bifurcation-induced and rate-induced tipping, and provides the first such analysis of rate-driven AMOC risk in a coupled climate model. ResKMD for stochastic bifurcation warning, classical rate-tipping indicators, learned rate-tipping classifiers, and AMOC transition predictors all predate this work. Reviewer inference: the defensible novelty is the explicit control-aware residual decomposition, its unusually important no-universal-divergence counterexample, and the bridge from prototypes to a small coupled-GCM ensemble. The contribution is mechanistic and hypothesis-generating rather than an operational AMOC alarm: only two positive GCM members, post hoc control sensitivity, and lack of calibrated thresholds leave the empirical claim preliminary.
reviewer_notes: The theorem, counterexample, prototype protocols, empirical examples, AMOC models, coupled-ensemble labels, spectral diagnostics, and forcing ablation were checked against the page-marked full text and supplement in a second pass. Author claims are reported separately from reviewer conclusions: the paper proves a conditional residual bound, not that every rate-induced tipping event must cause a warning. Competitive titles, identifiers, and scopes were checked on primary arXiv records.
